lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have already flashed both their promise and their flaws - one night they coughed up a lead, the next they tightened the screws and beat the Islanders 2-1. That win put them at 1-1-0, third in the Atlantic, with a little breathing room but no margin for drift. The headline here is Kirill Marchenko, whose move to the left side has been welcomed as a return to familiar ground, not some novelty act. John Chayka has also spent the week talking data, goaltending and Gavin McKenna, which tells you the organization is still building while trying to win now. Tonight's meeting with Ottawa is the next test - and the first chance to see whether this start was a reset or just a tease.

the_latest.headline: Leafs beat Islanders 2-1
the_latest.dek: Toronto snapped back after its season-opening loss and banked a needed early point swing in the Atlantic Division race. The 2-1 result also gave Jim Hiller his first win behind the bench and showed the Leafs can win a tighter, lower-scoring game.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season didn't end with a bang so much as a hard reset - and now the Blue Jays have to decide whether the structure around this club is sturdy enough to trust. The real story is the winter audit: second base is unsettled, Dylan Cease's shoulder needs managing, and management has already signaled that every part of the roster is under review. Toronto finished 79-83, 5th in the AL East, a record that leaves no room for nostalgia and plenty for correction. Cease's no-surgery diagnosis matters because an ace who struck out 239 batters over 169 innings can anchor a rotation; the question is whether his body cooperates. Elsewhere, the bat-and-glove balance at second base is unfinished business - the kind of hole that turns a middling club into a cleaner one. Watch the offseason moves at second base and in the rotation; that's where this team starts becoming relevant again.

the_latest.headline: Exploring Blue Jays' options at second base for next season
the_latest.dek: Toronto has not locked Ernie Clement into the job, which means second base is a real offseason decision rather than a placeholder. The answer will shape how aggressively the Blue Jays chase offense, defense, or both as they try to rebound from a fourth straight losing season.

the_latest.dek: Toronto's front office is treating this collapse as an offseason reset after a 79-83 finish and a fifth-place AL East result. The club went from a World Series run last year to missing the playoffs, so every roster decision now carries real weight.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The buzz in Quebec City is less about the preseason opener than the shape of the Raptors themselves - how quickly a team can turn camp theater into a real rotation. Darko Rajakovic's playful one-on-one with Kawhi Leonard, and the coach's admission that Leonard's Saturday status is still being handled carefully, became the defining image of camp. Toronto gets the Heat tonight, but the deeper countdown runs to Oct. 21 and the Bulls, when the games count for good. Leonard has looked active, if controlled, and the old broadcaster's chair will be filled again too, with Jack Armstrong back on TSN. That matters because a club this unfinished needs a steady voice. What to watch next: who grabs the final spots, how much Leonard can handle, and whether this roster looks ready before the opener.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: One win can change the mood in a building - and Washington finally has one, though it comes with a warning label. The Commanders' 33-31 escape over Seattle snapped the skid and left them 1-2, third in the NFC East, still only a game back and very much in the scrum. But the victory didn't calm the room; it sharpened the concern. Terry McLaurin was added to the final injury report with a hamstring issue and is questionable for London, and Marcus Mariota is still steering the offense with Jayden Daniels out. That's the edge here: a team that can finish, but can't afford to lose its best playmaker. Sunday morning against Indianapolis will tell whether this rebound has legs - or just borrowed time.

article.title: Leafs Open With Senators at Home
paragraphs: The Leafs open against Ottawa tonight at 7 p.m. at Scotiabank Arena, with Anthony Stolarz in goal and Linus Ullmark projected for the Senators. Toronto is 1-1-0, and the game is on Sportsnet.

The Blue Jays are already in offseason mode, and the focus is shifting to second base for next year after a season that ended earlier than hoped. The Raptors close camp with a preseason game against the Heat tonight at 7, while coach Darko Rajakovic waits on a few banged-up bodies, including Battle, Anderson, Graves and Bittle. The Commanders head to London to face the Colts on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. on NFL Net, with Keenan Allen listed questionable after missing Friday's practice.
